svg.aria-label: Diagram: how service agents differ from user-managed and default service accounts, the Service Agent Manager that writes role grants into your project policy and is visible only in audit logs, the drift loop this creates for policy-as-code, and why the email address format cannot be relied on
svg.title: Service agents: principals in your allow policy that you did not create
svg.text: Service agents: principals in your policy that you did not create.
Created by Google, granted roles by an identity visible only in audit logs, holding permissions that can change.
Three kinds of service account, and only two of them are yours
Kind
Created by
Managed by
On the IAM page by default
User-managed
You
You
Yes
Default
Google, on service enable
You
Yes
Service agent
Google
Google
No
A default service account is created for you but is still user-managed — you are responsible for it.
A service agent is neither created nor managed by you, and does not live in your project at all.
Your allow policy has a second author
service-agent-manager@system.gserviceaccount.com sets the allow policy on your project.
Google states it is visible only in audit logs. Not on the IAM page. Not in your Terraform state.
Service agents themselves are also not listed on the IAM page by default, even holding a role.
To see them at all, select the Include Google-provided role grants checkbox.
The loop this creates for policy-as-code
1. Google grants an agent a role. It appears in the real policy, not in your stored copy of it.
2. Your config does not include it, so those roles are revoked when you apply your configuration.
3. Some Google Cloud services will no longer work — with no signal that identity was the cause.
And pre-creating agents inverts the default: ones created at your request get NO automatic roles.
What the email address will not tell you
Both the creation time and the email address format for service agents are subject to change.
Compute Engine is compute-system. Cloud Run is serverless-robot-prod. Neither matches gcp-sa-*.
My own count of the reference table, 30 Sep 2026: 296 of 328 addresses on a gcp-sa-* domain.
The role is open-ended too: the permissions within these roles can change without notice.
So a service agent binding is not a grant you sized. It is a grant Google can resize.
Every post since #31 treated the project allow policy as a document you author. It is one you
co-author, with a party that does not file change requests.
